claims.text: The trip record shows the dropoff pin was amended after booking, at 09:27:40, and stores an amended optimal of 11.0 km / 19 min that is identical to the booked optimal of 11.0 km / 19 min (EV-TRIP-00702). POL-RD-05 requires POL-RD-01 to be re-run on the amended endpoints, and on those endpoints the pin move the driver proposed added no distance and no time whatsoever - so nothing in the amendment itself supports charging the rider more.

The driver's own GPS trace confirms the amendment was costless: trace_distance_km is 10.99 km against an optimal of 11.0 km, an excess of -0.01 km (-0.091%), far below POL-RD-01's 20% and 0.8 km gates, and the trace is complete - 100% coverage, 115 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps (EV-GPS-00702). There is no extra distance and no extra time on this record that the platform could bill, so the +SGD 8.60 re-quote rests on nothing in this trip's geometry.

The inducement is on the trip's own chat log, admitted at weight 1.0 with no issue codes (EV-CHAT-00702): at 09:26:50 the driver wrote 'Just move the pin to Block B, same price.', and at 09:27:45 the rider answered that the app now said 22.40, not 13.80. The only booking-time fare figure anywhere in the bundle is the 13.80 the rider was on when she moved the pin in reliance on that assurance; the bundle carries no other pre-amendment quote.

POL-RD-11 fixes this rider's fare at the figure fixed at booking and entitles her to the amount by which charged_total exceeds that figure, under POL-RD-11(a). The ledger records charged_total 22.40 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, with a quoted_fare_sgd of 22.40 that is nothing but the disputed post-amendment re-quote (EV-FARE-00702); measured against the booking-time fare of 13.80 recorded contemporaneously in the chat (EV-CHAT-00702) the excess is SGD 8.60 - the whole of the contested amount - and should be refunded in full.

Nothing offsets that refund: the fare ledger carries zero ERP, zero tolls, zero airport surcharge and zero waiting-time fee, and the trip did not originate at an airport (EV-FARE-00702). There is no pass-through or statutory line properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 to be netted against the rider's claim, and no off-route or phantom gantry line for the platform to defend.

If the tribunal concludes it cannot tell from this record which quote governed, the two accounts are admissible, mutually contradictory and of comparable strength - the rider's admitted chat at 13.80 and the ledger at 22.40, each at weight 1.0 - so POL-RD-10 requires escalation rather than a finding that leaves the rider carrying the charge, because escalation holds the disputed SGD 8.60 rather than collecting it.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-00702-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, which I disclose. No advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, so POL-RD-03 exoneration is unavailable on this record and no external traffic cause can dilute or reduce what is owed to the rider.

claims.text: The governing measurement shows no deviation at all. The driver's trace measures 10.99 km against a platform optimal of 11.0 km, so the excess is minus 0.01 km: the actual route is shorter than the optimal, not longer. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 test — an excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms — therefore fail, and POL-RD-01 provides that where either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The dropoff point was amended after booking — trip_record.dropoff_amended_at is 2026-09-22T09:27:40 — so POL-RD-05 requires POL-RD-01 to be re-run against the amended endpoints. The stored amended optimal is 11.0 km over 19.0 minutes, and the trace's 10.99 km sits below it. No deviation survives the recomputation, and POL-RD-05 states in terms that if no deviation survives the recomputation the outcome is NO_ACTION. POL-RD-05 also provides that distance driven before the amendment timestamp is never counted as excess against the driver.

The amendment was the rider's own act and the chat log says so. The rider's message records that after she changed the destination pin the app showed the amended figure; the driver's earlier message is a statement about price, not a platform-performed amendment. That is precisely the POL-RD-05 situation of a rider-moved dropoff pin, and it is the rider's edit, not anything the driver did to the route, that produced the figure she now disputes.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip — derived.money.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is non-null — so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the trip is driven. POL-RD-11 is the governing clause: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, the rider is already whole on those lines, and the loss from any detour falls on the driver. POL-RD-11 expressly closes the distance-refund route the rider's claim is built on.

Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's only monetary remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus properly chargeable pass-through lines. Here charged_total is SGD 22.40 and quoted_fare_sgd is SGD 22.40: the charged-over-quote figure is SGD 0.00 and the published POL-RD-11 remedy is SGD 0.00. There is nothing to refund on the arithmetic the policy prescribes.

The rider's assertion that the app re-quoted from SGD 13.80 to SGD 22.40 is not borne out by the ledger. The only quote recorded on the fare_breakdown is SGD 22.40, no SGD 13.80 quote appears on any admitted artifact, and the charged total equals the recorded quote. Since POL-RD-11 confines the rider's remedies to the over-quote amount and pass-through corrections, and neither is present, the contested SGD 8.60 has no basis in the record.

No pass-through correction is due under POL-RD-09. The fare_breakdown lists no ERP gantries, tolls_erp is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00 and waiting_time_fee is 0.00, and the properly_chargeable total is 0.00. There is accordingly no off-route gantry, no phantom charge line and no wrongly applied surcharge for the platform to correct on this trip.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. She must point to an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace, and this trace is unimpaired: 100% coverage, 115 fixes, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. It shows an excess of minus 0.01 km. The burden never shifts to the driver, who is therefore not put to any exculpatory clause at all.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established against the driver under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 250 — a ratio of 0.000 — so neither the count of 3 or more nor the ratio of 0.05 or more is met, and the clause's uplift and referral have no application here.

No driver compensation arises on this trip under POL-RD-04's second limb. That limb pays only where the fare_breakdown bills the rider for less distance than the gps_trace records and the shortfall exceeds 1.0 km. Here the billed 11.0 km is above the trace's 10.99 km, so there is no unbilled distance and nothing to compensate; the driver does not seek, and is not owed, any payment.

NO_ACTION is the correct outcome and it is a win for the driver here. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION leaves payment_status and refund_issued_sgd as they are: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION leaves the SGD 22.40 charge standing in full rather than restoring or increasing anything.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your claim is upheld. To the driver: no route deviation is found against you on this trip; the money refunded to the rider comes from the platform fare, not from your earnings.

ROUTE. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00702) is complete — 100% coverage, 115 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps — and measures 10.99 km against a platform optimal of 11.00 km, an excess of −0.01 km (−0.09%). Neither POL-RD-01 gate (excess above 20% of optimal, and above 0.80 km) is met, so no route deviation exists, and the dropoff-pin amendment at 09:27:40 does not change that: re-run on the amended endpoints under POL-RD-05, the stored amended optimal is 11.00 km / 19 min (identical to the booked optimal) and the trace again sits below it. The driver's traffic explanation under POL-RD-03 has no advisory to stand on — EV-ADVIS-00702-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, disclosed by the rider — and nothing turns on it, because there is no measured deviation to exonerate.

FARE. The trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE (fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd non-null), so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available; POL-RD-11 governs. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider recovers the amount by which charged_total exceeds the fare fixed at booking. The fare fixed at booking was SGD 13.80, recorded contemporaneously in the trip's own chat log (EV-CHAT-00702, weight 1.0): at 09:26:50 the driver wrote 'Just move the pin to Block B, same price', and at 09:27:45 the rider reported the app now said 22.40, not 13.80. The pin move was costless — the amended optimal equals the booked optimal — so the re-quote to SGD 22.40 has no distance or time behind it. Charged_total SGD 22.40 less the booking fare SGD 13.80 = SGD 8.60, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 8.60, which is the whole of the contested amount (SGD 8.60) and is returned in full. No pass-through correction is added or netted: no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge and no waiting-time fee (properly_chargeable total SGD 0.00).

The driver's contrary points. The assertion that 'no SGD 13.80 quote appears on any admitted artifact' is not correct: the chat log is an admitted artifact at weight 1.0 and it carries the figure. The platform's own ledger shows quoted_fare_sgd = charged_total = SGD 22.40 (charged_over_quote SGD 0.00), but that quoted figure is the disputed post-amendment re-quote; POL-RD-11 fixes the fare at booking, and the booking fare is what the refund is measured against. The driver otherwise succeeds on the points that do not move money: no repeat-deviation pattern (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250), so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral; and no driver compensation under POL-RD-04, because the billed 11.0 km is not less than the trace's 10.99 km and there is no unbilled distance.

The rider's request to escalate under POL-RD-10(7) is declined: the ledger's SGD 22.40 records the re-quote rather than a competing booking quote, and the driver's own 'same price' message corroborates the rider, so the two records are not mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength. As an open observation (not a referral), the platform may wish to review why a distance-neutral pin move triggered an SGD 8.60 re-quote.

Confidence 0.85, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts (EV-CHAT-00702 for the booking fare and the driver's assurance, EV-FARE-00702 for the charged total).

To the rider and the driver: the rider is entitled to the whole of the SGD 8.60 she contests.

What is not in dispute: the destination pin was moved mid-trip (dropoff_amended_at 2026-09-22T09:27:40) and the platform issued a new fare. The route itself is clean. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00702) has 100% coverage, 115 fixes at a 10 s cadence and no gaps, and measures 10.99 km against an optimal of 11.0 km; the amended optimal stored on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00702) is also 11.0 km / 19 min, identical to the booked optimal. Moving the pin about 80 m added no distance and no time, so there is no deviation under POL-RD-01, none survives the POL-RD-05 re-run, and no distance or time refund is available on an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip because POL-RD-02 does not run (POL-RD-11).

The disputed question is what the fare was fixed at before the move. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00702) records quoted_fare_sgd 22.40 and charged_total 22.40, so its own POL-RD-11(a) figure is 0.00. But the ledger was written at 09:38:00, after the 09:27:40 amendment, and the driver's own statement concedes that 'the platform issued the new quote'. The 22.40 on the ledger is therefore the post-amendment re-quote, not the figure fixed at booking that POL-RD-11(a) protects. The booking figure is recorded contemporaneously in the trip's chat log (EV-CHAT-00702, admitted at weight 1.0 with no issue codes): at 09:26:50 the driver wrote 'Just move the pin to Block B, same price', and at 09:27:45 the rider replied 'I changed it and the app now says 22.40, not 13.80'. The rider was on SGD 13.80.

Applying POL-RD-11(a): charged_total SGD 22.40 less the fare fixed at booking SGD 13.80 = SGD 8.60, refunded in full (well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and the whole contested amount). Nothing offsets it: the ledger carries no ERP or toll lines, no airport surcharge (the trip did not originate at an airport) and no waiting-time fee, and the properly chargeable total is SGD 0.00, so POL-RD-09 gives no standalone correction and no deduction.

On the arguments raised. I accept that the trace shows no deviation and that the rider edited the pin herself, but the driver's assurance of 'same price' in the same chat is why this fare consequence falls on the platform rather than the rider. I do not accept the driver's assertion that no SGD 13.80 figure appears on any admitted artifact: it appears in the rider's message on the chat log. I accept that no repeat-deviation pattern exists (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 250 completed trips), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral follows, and that no driver compensation arises (billed 11.0 km is not below the traced 10.99 km, POL-RD-04). The rider's alternative request that the case be escalated as undecidable under POL-RD-10 is declined: the driver's concession that a new quote was issued resolves which quote the ledger holds, so the record decides the case. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00702-01, weight 0.0) is noted, but no traffic cause was asserted, so POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-13 have nothing to work on; no charge line is unmatched, so POL-RD-09(4) produces no billing-integrity referral.

The finding rests on the chat log, the artifact that carries the deciding booking-fare fact, admitted at weight 1.0; confidence is set at 0.80, above the 0.70 floor.

To both parties: this route-deviation dispute is decided on the fare record, and it ends with the SGD 22.40 charge standing. NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status (CHARGED) and refund_issued_sgd (0.00) exactly as they are.

No deviation exists. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00702) runs 10.99 km against the platform optimal of 11.0 km — an excess of -0.01 km (-0.09%). That fails both of POL-RD-01's gates (more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km), so no deviation is established and the outcome is NO_ACTION. The trace is unimpaired: 100% coverage, 115 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps. The dropoff pin was amended at 09:27:40; re-running POL-RD-01 against the amended endpoints under POL-RD-05 gives the same answer — amended optimal 11.0 km / 19 min, trace 10.99 km — so no deviation survives the recomputation, and what POL-RD-05 says for that case is NO_ACTION. The rider's two points that the pin move added nothing and the trace is clean are therefore accepted; they simply do not generate a refund.

Why the fare does not move. The trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run: no distance-or-time refund is available however the trip was driven. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's only money is the amount by which charged_total (SGD 22.40) exceeds quoted_fare_sgd (SGD 22.40) plus properly chargeable pass-throughs — that is SGD 0.00. The fare breakdown carries no ERP, no tolls, no airport surcharge and no waiting-time fee, so nothing is due under POL-RD-09 and there is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4).

The claimed SGD 13.80 quote. The rider says the app re-quoted from SGD 13.80 to SGD 22.40 and asks for the SGD 8.60 difference. The figure 13.80 appears in the bundle only in the rider's own chat message of 09:27:45 (EV-CHAT-00702); no platform artifact records a 13.80 quote. POL-RD-11 defines the rider's remedy by fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd, which is 22.40, and POL-RD-05's note forbids a judge from inventing a re-quote. I cannot therefore treat 13.80 as the governing quote, and the SGD 8.60 over-charge is not made out. The driver's chat assurance 'same price' is consistent with the record on that footing.

The request to escalate. The rider asks for escalation under POL-RD-10 on the ground that the two accounts conflict. Declined. The fare question is one the policy answers by naming the field, so the conflict is resolved by the clause rather than escalated. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown; the trace is unimpaired; the timestamps agree; no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing artifact (no traffic cause was asserted, so the MISSING advisory EV-ADVIS-00702-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction); the refund does not exceed the ceiling; and every fare line has a counterpart in the trip record.

Driver's points. No repeat-deviation pattern can be built (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral applies. No driver compensation arises either: the fare bills 11.0 km against a 10.99 km trace, so there is no unbilled distance over the 1.0 km threshold.

Confidence is 0.85, capped at 1.0 because every deciding fact is carried by a full-weight artifact (EV-TRIP-00702, EV-GPS-00702, EV-FARE-00702).

One open question for the platform, which is not a referral and does not change the ruling: the rider's recollection of a 13.80 quote is unexplained by the record, and the platform may wish to check whether an earlier quote was displayed to her.

Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's only money is the amount by which charged_total (SGD 22.40) exceeds quoted_fare_sgd (SGD 22.40) plus properly chargeable pass-throughs — that is SGD 0.00. The claimed SGD 13.80 quote. The rider says the app re-quoted from SGD 13.80 to SGD 22.40 and asks for the SGD 8.60 difference. ruling.explanation: To both parties: I cannot decide this one on the record, so it goes to a human reviewer and the contested SGD 8.60 is held — neither collected nor refunded. Here is why. ROUTE. The route itself is not in dispute. The driver's GPS trace measures 10.99 km against a platform optimal of 11.0 km (EV-GPS-00702, EV-TRIP-00702), so there is no excess distance at all, let alone one meeting POL-RD-01's gates of more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km. The destination pin was moved at 09:27:40 and the stored amended optimal is still 11.0 km over 19 min, so re-running the test on the amended endpoints under POL-RD-05 leaves no deviation either. On distance, the driver is right and no distance refund is available. FARE. This was an upfront-quoted trip (EV-FARE-00702), so POL-RD-11 governs and the only money question is whether the amount charged exceeds the fare fixed at booking. Two records of comparable weight disagree on what that fare was. The fare ledger records quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 22.40 against a charge of SGD 22.40 — equal, so POL-RD-11(a)'s arithmetic gives SGD 0.00 and no refund can be read off the fare breakdown. But the rider's in-app message, sent at 09:27:45 from inside the trip, records the app showing SGD 13.80 immediately before the pin was moved and SGD 22.40 immediately after (EV-CHAT-00702), and the driver's own statement concedes that 'the platform issued the new quote.' At face value the rider is SGD 8.60 out of pocket; on the recorded quote she is not. The driver's assertion that no SGD 13.80 figure appears on any admitted artifact is not correct — it appears in the chat log, which is admitted at weight 1.0. ESCALATION. Both sides are therefore supported by admissible, mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength (both weight 1.0) on the single fact that decides the money — which quoted fare was fixed at booking. That is the POL-RD-10(7) trigger, and it is terminal: no monetary outcome issues. What would resolve it is the platform's own booking-time quote record for this trip (the pre-amendment quote), which is not in the bundle. OTHER POINTS, none of which change the outcome. No repeat-deviation pattern is established (0 flags in 90 days over 250 trips, POL-RD-06), so no driver-conduct referral is made and none of POL-RD-06(a)-(c) fires. No ERP, toll, airport-surcharge or waiting-time line exists to correct (POL-RD-09), and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4). The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00702-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) changes nothing, because no party relied on an external traffic cause (POL-RD-13). No unbilled-distance compensation is due (POL-RD-04).

ledger.claim: The trip record shows the dropoff pin was amended after booking, at 09:27:40, and stores an amended optimal of 11.0 km / 19 min that is identical to the booked optimal of 11.0 km / 19 min (EV-TRIP-00702). POL-RD-05 requires POL-RD-01 to be re-run on the amended endpoints, and on those endpoints the pin move the driver proposed added no distance and no time whatsoever - so nothing in the amendment itself supports charging the rider more.

The driver's own GPS trace confirms the amendment was costless: trace_distance_km is 10.99 km against an optimal of 11.0 km, an excess of -0.01 km (-0.091%), far below POL-RD-01's 20% and 0.8 km gates, and the trace is complete - 100% coverage, 115 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps (EV-GPS-00702). There is no extra distance and no extra time on this record that the platform could bill, so the +SGD 8.60 re-quote rests on nothing in this trip's geometry.

The inducement is on the trip's own chat log, admitted at weight 1.0 with no issue codes (EV-CHAT-00702): at 09:26:50 the driver wrote 'Just move the pin to Block B, same price.', and at 09:27:45 the rider answered that the app now said 22.40, not 13.80. The only booking-time fare figure anywhere in the bundle is the 13.80 the rider was on when she moved the pin in reliance on that assurance; the bundle carries no other pre-amendment quote.

POL-RD-11 fixes this rider's fare at the figure fixed at booking and entitles her to the amount by which charged_total exceeds that figure, under POL-RD-11(a). The ledger records charged_total 22.40 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, with a quoted_fare_sgd of 22.40 that is nothing but the disputed post-amendment re-quote (EV-FARE-00702); measured against the booking-time fare of 13.80 recorded contemporaneously in the chat (EV-CHAT-00702) the excess is SGD 8.60 - the whole of the contested amount - and should be refunded in full.

Nothing offsets that refund: the fare ledger carries zero ERP, zero tolls, zero airport surcharge and zero waiting-time fee, and the trip did not originate at an airport (EV-FARE-00702). There is no pass-through or statutory line properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 to be netted against the rider's claim, and no off-route or phantom gantry line for the platform to defend.

If the tribunal concludes it cannot tell from this record which quote governed, the two accounts are admissible, mutually contradictory and of comparable strength - the rider's admitted chat at 13.80 and the ledger at 22.40, each at weight 1.0 - so POL-RD-10 requires escalation rather than a finding that leaves the rider carrying the charge, because escalation holds the disputed SGD 8.60 rather than collecting it.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-00702-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, which I disclose. No advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, so POL-RD-03 exoneration is unavailable on this record and no external traffic cause can dilute or reduce what is owed to the rider.

The governing measurement shows no deviation at all. The driver's trace measures 10.99 km against a platform optimal of 11.0 km, so the excess is minus 0.01 km: the actual route is shorter than the optimal, not longer. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 test — an excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms — therefore fail, and POL-RD-01 provides that where either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The dropoff point was amended after booking — trip_record.dropoff_amended_at is 2026-09-22T09:27:40 — so POL-RD-05 requires POL-RD-01 to be re-run against the amended endpoints. The stored amended optimal is 11.0 km over 19.0 minutes, and the trace's 10.99 km sits below it. No deviation survives the recomputation, and POL-RD-05 states in terms that if no deviation survives the recomputation the outcome is NO_ACTION. POL-RD-05 also provides that distance driven before the amendment timestamp is never counted as excess against the driver.

The amendment was the rider's own act and the chat log says so. The rider's message records that after she changed the destination pin the app showed the amended figure; the driver's earlier message is a statement about price, not a platform-performed amendment. That is precisely the POL-RD-05 situation of a rider-moved dropoff pin, and it is the rider's edit, not anything the driver did to the route, that produced the figure she now disputes.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip — derived.money.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is non-null — so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the trip is driven. POL-RD-11 is the governing clause: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, the rider is already whole on those lines, and the loss from any detour falls on the driver. POL-RD-11 expressly closes the distance-refund route the rider's claim is built on.

Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's only monetary remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus properly chargeable pass-through lines. Here charged_total is SGD 22.40 and quoted_fare_sgd is SGD 22.40: the charged-over-quote figure is SGD 0.00 and the published POL-RD-11 remedy is SGD 0.00. There is nothing to refund on the arithmetic the policy prescribes.

The rider's assertion that the app re-quoted from SGD 13.80 to SGD 22.40 is not borne out by the ledger. The only quote recorded on the fare_breakdown is SGD 22.40, no SGD 13.80 quote appears on any admitted artifact, and the charged total equals the recorded quote. Since POL-RD-11 confines the rider's remedies to the over-quote amount and pass-through corrections, and neither is present, the contested SGD 8.60 has no basis in the record.

No pass-through correction is due under POL-RD-09. The fare_breakdown lists no ERP gantries, tolls_erp is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00 and waiting_time_fee is 0.00, and the properly_chargeable total is 0.00. There is accordingly no off-route gantry, no phantom charge line and no wrongly applied surcharge for the platform to correct on this trip.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. She must point to an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace, and this trace is unimpaired: 100% coverage, 115 fixes, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. It shows an excess of minus 0.01 km. The burden never shifts to the driver, who is therefore not put to any exculpatory clause at all.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established against the driver under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 250 — a ratio of 0.000 — so neither the count of 3 or more nor the ratio of 0.05 or more is met, and the clause's uplift and referral have no application here.

No driver compensation arises on this trip under POL-RD-04's second limb. That limb pays only where the fare_breakdown bills the rider for less distance than the gps_trace records and the shortfall exceeds 1.0 km. Here the billed 11.0 km is above the trace's 10.99 km, so there is no unbilled distance and nothing to compensate; the driver does not seek, and is not owed, any payment.

NO_ACTION is the correct outcome and it is a win for the driver here. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION leaves payment_status and refund_issued_sgd as they are: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so on this rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION leaves the SGD 22.40 charge standing in full rather than restoring or increasing anything.
